title: What We Still Have to Solve

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What We Still Have to Solve treats global challenges as interacting systems.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A hospital’s ordinary morning already depends on energy, water, logistics, information, and trust.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks how solving one bottleneck can create another dependency.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central direction is a civilization able to detect mistakes and change course.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers gain a way to connect technical possibilities with the institutions needed to make them work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A hospital can contain capable clinicians while a failure in another service disrupts its work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its dependence on power, water, supplies, and communication belongs inside the analysis of care.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book uses this ordinary setting to show how consequences travel between institutional categories.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Improving one component may create a new vulnerability at the interface.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That makes the unit of analysis a connected service rather than a department’s isolated success.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The broader chapters distinguish physical limits, missing knowledge, institutional incentives, and coordination failures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Technical capability does not decide which risks are acceptable or who should bear their costs.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The constructive direction emphasizes feedback, plural experiments, graceful failure, and the ability to recover.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It preserves the possibility that future problems will escape today’s catalogue.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers encounter a framework for continued learning rather than a final master plan for civilization.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Begin with the hospital’s morning, then follow the distinction between kinds of unsolved problems.
